subject: Origins to Outcomes: OKR storyboard & field notes for QBR
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Origins to Outcomes: OKR storyboard & field notes for QBR

Team —

Attached is a lightweight storyboard I sketched overnight to help frame the QBR narrative. Purpose is to: 1) connect the original hypothesis behind our OKRs ("origins") to what actually moved the needle ("outcomes"); and 2) call out the three signal moments we should present to execs.

High level asks:
- Can each of you add 1 short example (2–3 bullets) that maps an OKR to a concrete customer / technical signal in the attached CSV by EOD.
- Vivek: recommend which of the six graded marks we keep as-is vs. convert to qualitative "needs follow-up".
- Laura: I'll need a two-line lead paragraph for the QBR slide deck by 3pm.

Notes on format: we want crisp cause→effect pairs, and we should avoid re-stating metrics without context (what changed behavior, what we learned, and next step). External partners (Amanda, Raj) are on the thread to confirm the signal moments that reference their pilots.

Attachments: qbr_storyboard_v1.pdf (sketch slides), field_notes_q1.csv (mapping doc).

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Origins to Outcomes: OKR storyboard & field notes for QBR

Irene —

Reviewed the storyboard. I pushed a short paragraph into the doc: two-line hook + context for the Platform reliability OKR (latency P95 reductions). Quick examples I added to the CSV:
- Customer X observed 15% lower median latency after rollout (pilot channel).
- Autoscaler tuning reduced queue depth, which dropped observed tail latency spikes.

Open question: for the reliability OKR I propose we keep the numeric grade but add a short rationale line — that preserves comparability for execs while making it actionable.

I'll continue filling the other OKRs and aim to finish my examples by 1pm.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Engineering Operations

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Origins to Outcomes: OKR storyboard & field notes for QBR

Thanks, Irene and Laura. Two quick framing suggestions from leadership:

1) Keep a single canonical "grade" per OKR for the slide deck, but surface the qualitative caveats in the appendix ("grade + 1-line caveat"). Avoid creating a new taxonomy — execs want to scan.
2) For any OKR with external dependencies (Acme pilot, AtlasAI integration), include one sentence on whether the dependency is on-time / at-risk.

From my side: for three OKRs I suggest converting numeric grades into "At Target / Needs Follow-up" instead of 1–5, because the underlying data is noisy this quarter. I'll mark which ones in the CSV and add a one-line rationale.

Also — Laura, if you can keep your lead paragraph to plain English (no internal shorthand), that'll help Melissa and the board.

Vivek
VP Product Strategy

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Origins to Outcomes: OKR storyboard & field notes for QBR

Adding my examples and a short retrospective note for the "Adoption" objective. Key signals I added to the CSV:
- Field trial with Acme: two teams adopted Redwood API extensions; time-to-first-call dropped from 3 days to 20 hours.
- Internal inference cost per query rose 4% because of unexpected long-tail sequences — we treated this as a learning and implemented a 1-week caching pilot.

Proposed action items (short):
- C1: Expand Acme pilot to one additional team to validate scale (owner: Amanda; target: Apr 15).
- C2: Launch a short A/B on prefix caching for long-tail queries (owner: Infra).

I attached a cleaned CSV slice and a 1-page note in the drive link.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Origins to Outcomes: OKR storyboard & field notes for QBR

Great work everyone — thank you for the fast turn. Quick synthesis and next steps before I hand this to the slides team: 

Synthesis (to use on slide 2):
- Origins: We set OKRs based on three bets — (A) predictable latency economics, (B) enterprise adoption via on-prem pilots, (C) cost reduction through cache + quantization.
- Outcomes: Signals show partial wins on A and B, with C delayed due to long-tail workload variance.
- Leadership ask: endorse three tactical pilots (Acme expansion, prefix caching A/B, autoscaler tuning roadmap) and allow 2 weeks of focused instrumentation work for better grade confidence.

Final asks / deliverables:
- Laura: two-line executive lead (due 3pm PT tomorrow).
- Marissa: confirm owners and dates in the CSV (complete by EOD).
- Vivek: mark the three OKRs you want re-labeled "Needs Follow-up"; include 1-line caveat each.

Amanda / Raj — quick confirm: are you comfortable with the two signal moments referencing your pilots being shared with the board slide deck? If yes, no reply needed; if not, flag here and we'll omit.

I'll pull the final packet together at 9am tomorrow and send to slides.

Thanks —
Irene
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
Attachments: qbr_storyboard_v1.pdf, field_notes_q1.csv
